title: BK09 full AES-256: first-stage 85-bit partial key recovery

target.description: The complete14-round AES-256 oracle is queried, but this endpoint stops at85 recovered bits of KA and separately85bits of KC. These correlated recovered materials are not170 independent master-key bits and do not constitute complete recovery.

setting.key_relation: Key-schedule-induced nonlinear relations defined in Section 5.1 and Figure 4, pp.8-9: manipulate the second subkey and a mixed intermediate key-schedule state, then invert the schedule. Not four fixed-XOR master keys.
setting.key_population: all keys as expressly claimed by the authors
setting.plaintext_model: chosen structures with adaptively modified ciphertexts
assumptions: Oracles for the paper's four specific related keys are available.
Adaptive encryption/decryption access follows the Section 5.2 algorithm.
The final key-recovery work estimate is author analysis rather than independently reproduced computation.

time.note: PDFp.11 source-reported overall first-stage2^99.5 time, dominated by oracle work; filtering alone is estimated2^77.5. No full-AES equivalence is supplied for the filtering budget.

data.note: Four encryption/decryption directions together; Section 5.2 uses 2^25.5 structures of 2^72 texts in each direction.

memory.note: PDFp.11 explicitly gives2^77.5 memory for this85-bit endpoint. Table1 belongs to the completed attack and is not substituted. Step4 count inconsistency leaves the derivation unresolved.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing budget is reported for this selected result.

success.description: Section5.2 expects about three right quartets and reports a local bound for three wrong quartets proposing the same candidates. Neither statement supplies the success of the85-bit recovery for KA and85-bit recovery for KC. Existing source joint-probability, Step4 candidate arithmetic and applicable memory disputes remain unchanged.

review.scope: Rechecked exact conference PDF8–17, including first-stage85-bit output, full-key completion, expected right-quartet counts, voting and the native AES192 failure/restart step. No numerical probability for the selected output at its listed native cost is established. Expected counts and local wrong-vote bounds do not fill this gap; published joint-probability, counting and memory disputes remain. Targeted endpoint success review, not a new full audit or attack reproduction.

PDF10: three active S-boxes in rounds10–14, each at2^-6. The ladder switch is excluded from this charge.
PDF10: author model2^(-30-30-18-18) for a boomerang quartet after the first round. The pre-existing probability-justification dispute is not resolved by recording this value.
PDF10 Step7: six-bit candidate-quartet filter from first-round and key-schedule S-box validity. This is not the later Step4 arithmetic.

PDF11: source upper bound for three wrong quartets proposing the same key candidates in the first-stage vote. It is not the probability of obtaining three right quartets or the full/partial recovery success.

Step4 quartet arithmetic and the published probability-justification dispute are retained without inventing corrected costs.

field_conflicts.label: Published probability-justification dispute
field_conflicts.description: Murphy explicitly questions the probability/data-demand justification of BK09. His concrete zero-probability AES example is a two-round single-key construction, not a counterexample to these full-round related-key trails. DEFN22 later continues to quote the historical BK09 estimates. Preserve the reported point with this dispute; neither automatic validation nor refutation is inferred.
